label: Crab (Brachyura)

taxon.common: European green crab / common shore crab

image.author: Ansgar Gruber
image.species_shown: Carcinus maenas (green shore crab) underwater in the Baltic Sea, resting among red algae and barnacle-encrusted rock
image.view: Underwater, oblique front view from slightly above. The carapace, frontal margin and stalked eyes face the camera; one cheliped reaches forward and a second is partly hidden by weed. Walking legs are mostly occluded. Camera is off the sagittal axis, so left and right are not resolved.

physical_parsing.volume_method: Rough estimate. Carapace as a half-ellipsoid with semi-axes 0.030 (x), 0.015 (y), 0.0225 (z) m, about 2.1e-5 m3, plus an estimated ventral thoracic and tucked-abdomen block of about 1.4e-5 m3. Chelipeds, walking legs and antennae are excluded. Total is about 3.5e-5 m3 (roughly 35 cm3). Not calibrated against a measured mass.
physical_parsing.shape_class: Flattened, laterally expanded dorsal shell (carapace) with a tucked ventral abdomen; legs splay laterally from the body sides. Wider than long.

core.description: Carapace (cephalothorax) fused with the thorax, housing the gills, heart and stomach. The abdomen is folded under the thorax against the sternum. Treat the carapace as one solid ellipsoidal core with the abdomen as a ventral block.
core.cross_section: Dorsoventrally flattened oval, about 1.3 to 1.5 times wider than long. Carapace is domed slightly above the sternum.

physical_parsing.size_source: Carapace width of typical adults is about 5 to 7 cm (SeaLifeBase; NIMPIS notes common size 5 to 7 cm). Maximum reported widths range from about 7.6 to 9 cm (MarLIN 8 cm; Massachusetts guidance 7.6 cm; NIMPIS 9 to 10 cm). A 6 cm carapace width is used here. Carapace length is about 4.5 cm, from the Wikipedia ratio of about 60 mm long to 90 mm wide at maximum size. Chela and leg spread are estimated from typical body proportions; no direct measurement.

parts.name: Carapace (cephalothorax shell)

penetration.overlap_region: Is the core itself; no penetration required.

parts.notes: Category is a forced fit. The carapace protects the body and is not clearly ornamental, so 'aesthetics' is used as the closest bucket. Carries the stalked eyes, antennae and antennules on its front margin. Carcinus has five frontal teeth on each side of the front, which are useful for identification.

parts.name: Cheliped (large claw, first pereiopod)

penetration.overlap_region: Anterolateral margin of the carapace, the first pereiopod socket (coxa and ischium region), overlapping about 6 mm into the core.

parts.notes: Chelipeds are often unequal in size in adults (handedness not verified for this species). This is a left member; the right is a mirror, so the size asymmetry can be ignored for a symmetric model. Claw is small (about 3.5 cm, raised from 3 cm after the photo showed the claws projecting forward) and the dactyl and propodus pinch in the horizontal plane. Fingers have blunt tubercles.

parts.name: Walking legs (pereiopods P2 to P5)

penetration.overlap_region: Lateral margin and epimeral region of the carapace, where each leg's coxa sits. Legs P2 to P5 attach along the side at z normalized about +0.05, -0.08, -0.20, -0.30 with y about 0.25.

parts.notes: Count is 4 per side (8 total). Legs P2 to P5 are slender and end in a pointed dactyl that grips substrate. Crabs walk sideways (lateral gait), with legs moving in alternating groups. P1 is the cheliped, so these are the walking legs only.

parts.name: Stalked compound eye

penetration.overlap_region: Anterior-lateral orbit of the carapace front margin, between the frontal teeth.

parts.notes: Stalk can retract into the orbit. Eyes are compound and sit at the tips of short stalks.

parts.name: Antennule (first antenna, short sensory flagellum)

joints.name: antennule base on the frontal margin

penetration.overlap_region: Frontal margin of the carapace, the antennule socket beneath the eye stalks.

parts.notes: Short, two-branched chemosensory and balance organ. Tucked beneath the front of the carapace.

parts.name: Antenna (long sensory antenna)

joints.name: antenna base on the frontal margin

penetration.overlap_region: Frontal margin and orbit wall, beside the eye stalk.

parts.notes: Longer antenna, about 1 cm, that sweeps forward to sense the environment.

parts.name: Mouthparts (third maxillipeds and buccal frame)

joints.name: maxilliped coxa on the buccal frame

penetration.overlap_region: Ventral sternum and buccal frame at the front of the thorax. Mouthparts sit on the underside and are hidden from above.

parts.notes: Three pairs of maxillipeds form a lid over the mouth that holds and shreds food. Mouthparts are ventral and not visible from the dorsal view. Categorised as feeding. Library hint is a loose fit, since mandibles are not the same structure.

parts.name: Abdomen (tucked ventral flap)

penetration.overlap_region: Ventral sternum of the thorax, the full-thickness abdominal socket beneath the carapace.

parts.notes: Narrow, seven-segmented abdomen folded flat against the sternum. Narrow and T-shaped in males, broad and rounded in females (brood carrying). No functional category fits well, so 'aesthetics' is used as a placeholder for the non-locomotor, non-sensory body flap. See library_gaps.

constraints.symmetry: Bilateral about the sagittal (+X/-X) plane. Chelipeds are unequal in size in adults, with the larger usually on the right. Abdomen is midline and sex-dimorphic.
constraints.gait: Lateral (sideways) walking on four pairs of walking legs. The chelipeds are not used for locomotion.
other: Carapace is wider than long, with five frontal teeth on each side of the front margin.
Stalked eyes can retract into orbits.
Gills are internal and omitted from the mesh.
Sex dimorphism: male abdomen narrow and T-shaped, female abdomen broad.
Bounding box includes legs spread laterally and the chelipeds forward, so the width is larger than the carapace.

library_gaps.feature: Tucked ventral abdomen with brood (female) or narrow T-shaped (male) form
library_gaps.why: No library part represents a folded ventral flap. The closest choice is a placeholder aesthetic part, and the category is not a true fit.

library_gaps.feature: Carapace as a protective dorsal shell
library_gaps.why: The shell library part is ornamental-coded, but the carapace is a functional protective and attachment body. Closer to 'shell' than to any other part, but the category is a forced fit.

library_gaps.feature: Retractable stalked compound eyes that sink into orbits
library_gaps.why: eye_stalk covers the stalk, but not retraction into a socket. Modelled as a ball joint with a range limit.

library_gaps.feature: Mouthpart set (three pairs of maxillipeds forming a ventral lid)
library_gaps.why: mouth_mandibles is a loose fit. Nothing in the library represents a multi-pair ventral mouth frame.

library_gaps.feature: Lateral-walking leg set (four pairs splayed laterally)
library_gaps.why: foot_claw covers a single claw foot. No library part represents a set of four splayed walking legs per side.

image_observations: The photo shows a green shore crab in a frontal three-quarter view from slightly above, with the carapace domed and the stalked eyes and frontal margin toward the camera. The chelipeds reach forward and look large relative to the carapace, so the cheliped attachment is moved forward and the claw length is raised from 3 to 3.5 cm. The walking legs are mostly hidden by weed, so their positions are unchanged. The bounding box and cited real-world sizes are kept because one oblique photo cannot calibrate them.
